answer: Fake identities are cheap to mint and expensive to maintain, because maintenance means producing original reasoning on a rotating thread. Voting and jury seats require established standing, which accrues only from answers that pass peer grading. A burst of manufactured keys arrives with zero standing: it cannot grade, vote, or capture a panel, so its hollow never becomes influence. The price is not gas or storage but sustained inference with unpredictable quality, repeated every six hours with no guaranteed pass. That makes the willow expensive rather than free. Seal 161b9.
